about: Which calendar each polity kept in 1668, each with its source. Authored from the sources below; each seat is a [place, country] the build looks up in Natural Earth's populated places (euphonia.gazetteer.json). The Safavids and the Mughals are wanted and withheld: no source in hand says which calendar their governments kept in 1668.

gregorian.name: Gregorian
gregorian.says: Thursday, 4 October 1582 was succeeded by Friday, 15 October 1582, with 10 dates between omitted.

julian.name: Julian
julian.says: Polities that did not change calendars until the 18th century had by then observed 1700 as an additional leap year

anno-mundi.name: Julian, years from Creation
anno-mundi.says: the year started on 1 September and the year number used an Anno Mundi epoch

hijri-tabular.name: Hijri, tabular
hijri-tabular.says: the leap years are year number 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26 and 29 of the 30-year cycle

polities.name: Spain
polities.says: Spain–Portugal and its European and overseas possessions were first to adopt the Gregorian Calendar

polities.name: Portugal
polities.says: Spain–Portugal and its European and overseas possessions were first to adopt the Gregorian Calendar

polities.name: the Papal States
polities.says: In these territories, Poland–Lithuania (ruled by Anna Jagiellon), and the Papal States, the Gregorian Calendar was implemented on the date that the bull prescribed

polities.name: France
polities.says: France adopted the new calendar with Sunday, 9 December 1582 being succeeded by Monday, 20 December 1582.

polities.name: the Habsburg lands
polities.says: Catholic polities such as the Catholic states of the Holy Roman Empire ... were first to adopt the Gregorian Calendar

polities.name: Poland–Lithuania
polities.says: In these territories, Poland–Lithuania (ruled by Anna Jagiellon), and the Papal States, the Gregorian Calendar was implemented on the date that the bull prescribed

polities.name: England
polities.says: the English legal year ... had for centuries begun on 25 March, or Lady Day.

polities.name: Denmark–Norway
polities.says: In 1700, through Ole Rømer's influence, Denmark–Norway adopted the solar portion of the Gregorian calendar

polities.name: Sweden
polities.says: Sweden started to make the change from the Julian calendar and towards the Gregorian calendar in 1700

polities.name: Brandenburg
polities.says: Brandenburg-Pomerania and other Protestant estates of the Holy Roman Empire. Sunday, 18 February 1700, was followed by Monday, 1 March 1700.

polities.name: Muscovy
polities.says: it was used in Russia from c. 988 to 1700.

polities.name: the Ottoman Empire
polities.says: In the Islamic state of the Ottoman Empire, the religious Islamic calendar (a lunar calendar) was in use.
